headline: ChatGPT can now create and edit animated GIFs
summary: OpenAI's latest update allows users to generate GIFs from prompts or photos, with options to adjust speed and edit frames.
details: ChatGPT has been updated to natively generate animated GIFs. Users can now create GIFs directly within the AI chatbot by providing a prompt or uploading a photo.
The new feature, part of OpenAI's Images 2.6 model rollout, offers granular control over the generated GIFs. Users can adjust the animation speed and edit individual frames.
This marks a significant expansion of ChatGPT's creative capabilities beyond static image generation. Previously, creating GIFs required external tools or complex workarounds.
OpenAI also reported a substantial increase in image generation, with users now creating over 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT and its API, up from 3 billion per week in September.

The Images 2.6 update is available to all ChatGPT and Codex users on web, desktop, and mobile applications. OpenAI is also introducing new API models, Flare and Sunburst, for enhanced image generation.
caption:
ChatGPT can now make animated GIFs from your prompts or photos, with full control over speed and frames.

ChatGPT has been updated to natively generate animated GIFs. Users can now create GIFs directly within the AI chatbot by providing a prompt or uploading a photo.

The new feature, part of OpenAI's Images 2.6 model rollout, offers granular control over the generated GIFs. Users can adjust the animation speed and edit individual frames.

This marks a significant expansion of ChatGPT's creative capabilities beyond static image generation. Previously, creating GIFs required external tools or complex workarounds.

OpenAI also reported a substantial increase in image generation, with users now creating over 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT and its API, up from 3 billion per week in September.

The Images 2.6 update is available to all ChatGPT and Codex users on web, desktop, and mobile applications. OpenAI is also introducing new API models, Flare and Sunburst, for enhanced image generation.
